title: Greet and introduce yourself
bridge: Sɛn Twi, yɛbɔ hwɛ akye yɛka 'Agoo' anaa 'Da yie', na sɛ yɛbɛma yɛn ho nhoma a, yɛka 'Me din de...'. Sɛn English nso, yɛbɔ hwɛ akye yɛka 'Hello' anaa 'Good morning', na yɛka 'My name is...' anaa 'I am...'. Nnini pii a ɛba ne sɛ, sɛn English yɛnntɔn 'I am called...' (ɣyɛ sɛ ɛyɛ kyerɛw foforo, na ɛtɔ da biara na ɛyɛ ɛho nhwɛso sɛn kwan ma wɔbɔ). Fa akɔntaba ma wɔn a, sɛn English yɛde 'to be' kyerɛkyerɛ ma yɛbisa din: 'What is your name?' (nnyɛ 'How are you called?').
rule: Bɔ hwɛ akye: 'Hello' (Agoo), 'Hi' (ɛho nhwɛso pii), 'Good morning' (Da yie), 'Good afternoon' (Ete sen), 'Good evening' (Ma wo ho yɛ). Ma wo ho nhoma: 'My name is...' (Me din de...) anaa 'I am...' (Mɛyɛ...). Bisa din: 'What is your name?' (Wode din deɛn?). Tɔ hwɛ akye: 'Nice to meet you' (Mepɛ wo) na tɔnso ne 'Nice to meet you too'. Faako: 'Goodbye', 'Bye', 'See you later'.

common_error.explanation: Sɛn Twi yɛka 'Me din de Anna', nanso sɛn English, kyerɛw a wɔde ma wɔma wɔn ho nhoma pii ne 'My name is...' anaa 'I am...'. 'I am called' yɛ kyerɛw foforo nso na ɛtɔ da biara na ɛyɛ ɛho nhwɛso sɛn kwan ma wɔbɔ.

examples.note: Bɔ hwɛ akye kyerɛw bi.
Kyerɛw bi ma woka wo din.
Bisa din kyerɛw bi.
Faako kyerɛw bi.

title: Ma yɛnkyɛ wo ntɛm (nsɛnkyerɛnne, abakɔsɛm, ɛsɔfo nkwan)
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka yɛn nsɛnkyerɛ a, yɛse: 'Mɛyɛ 25 nsɛn' (yɛnka ɛno 'yɛ'), nanso wɔ Gyeman nea ɛbɛyɛ ne: 'Mɛyɛ 25 nsɛn' (yɛnka ɛno 'be'). Ɛno a wɔka ho nhia wɔ abakɔsɛm no, yɛse: 'Mɛyɛ Amanfoɔ' (nni apamfoɔ), nanso wɔ Gyeman nea ɛbɛyɛ ne: 'Mɛyɛ Amanfoɔ' (nni apamfoɔ). Wɔ ɛsɔfo nkwan no, yɛse: 'Mɛyɛ ɛsɔfo' (nni apamfoɔ), nanso wɔ Gyeman nea ɛbɛyɛ ne: 'Mɛyɛ ɛsɔfo bi'.
rule: Nsɛnkyerɛnne: 'Mɛyɛ [nsɛn] nsɛn' (e.g. Mɛyɛ 25 nsɛn). Abakɔsɛm: 'Mɛyɛ [abakɔsɛm]' (e.g. Mɛyɛ Amanfoɔ, Mɛyɛ Mɛxikani). Ɛsɔfo nkwan: 'Mɛyɛ a/an [ɛsɔfo nkwan]' (e.g. Mɛyɛ adwumafo, Mɛyɛ enyimfoɔ). Kyɛw: 'Wo nsɛn ara na ɛyɛ?' (Wo nsɛn ara na ɛyɛ?), 'Ɛhe na woka?' (Ɛhe na woka?), 'Deɛ wo yɛ ne dɛn?' (Deɛ wo yɛ ne dɛn?) anaa 'Wo deɛ wo yɛ ne dɛn?'.

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, yɛse 'Mɛyɛ 25 nsɛn' yɛnka 'yɛ', nanso wɔ Gyeman nea ɛbɛyɛ ne: 'Mɛyɛ 25 nsɛn' yɛnka 'be'. Ɛyɛ anaa ɛha a wɔhyɛ wɔ Amanfoɔ.

examples.note: Yɛnka 'be' ma nsɛnkyerɛnne.
Nni apamfoɔ ma abakɔsɛm.
Kɔ apamfoɔ 'a' anaa 'an' ma ɛsɔfo nkwan.
Kyɛw ho nhia wɔ ɛhe.

title: Bɛma abɛntenn kɛ wɔn a wɔde kɔ so (ntɛm basic)
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛma abɛntenn kɛ wɔn a wɔde kɔ so, yɛde adwumafo no hyɛn saa ɛbɛn: 'trotrɔ a ɛyɛ den', 'baabi a ɛyɛ papa'. Wɔ English, adwumafo no kɔ so ɛkɛse ɛbɛn no: 'a red car', 'a tall girl'. Yɛn na yɛde 'to be' verb no ma yɛbɛma wɔn a wɛn kɔ so (She is tall) na yɛde 'have got' ma yɛbɛma wɔn a wɔn ho adwuma (She has got blue eyes).
rule: Sɛ yɛbɛma: 1) Adwumafo + ɛbɛn (a big house). 2) Abusuafo + 'to be' verb no + adwumafo (The house is big). 3) Abusuafo + 'have/has got' + adwuma a wɔwɔ ho (She has got long hair). Adwumafo a wɔn ho nhɔ: big (papa), small (ntɛm), tall (kɔkɔ), short (kɔkɔntɛm), beautiful (sɛn), old (mmarima), young (mmarima ntɛm), fast (ntɛm), slow (kɔkɔ).

concept_examples.translation: Woi yɛ ɛbɛn a ɛyɛ papa.

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi, adwumafo no kɔ so ɛbɛn no ('trotrɔ a ɛyɛ den'), nanso wɔ English, adwumafo no kɔ ɛkɛse ɛbɛn no ('a red car'). Ɛyɛ nkɔnsɔnni a ɛso wɔn a wɔde Twi.

examples.note: Adwumafo no kɔ so ɛbɛn no.
Yɛde 'to be' verb no ma yɛbɛma wɔn a wɛn kɔ so.

levels.label: have/has got for features
levels.translation: have/has got ma adwuma a wɔwɔ ho

examples.note: Yɛde 'have got' ma yɛbɛma wɔn a wɔn ho adwuma.

examples.original: My brother is young and he has got green eyes.
examples.phonetic: /maɪ ˈbrʌðə ɪz jʌŋ ænd hiː hæz ɡɒt ɡriːn aɪz/
examples.translation: Me mma no yɛ mmarima ntɛm na ɔwɔ adwuma a ɛyɛ den.
examples.note: Ntɛm a ɛyɛ 'to be' na 'have got'.

title: Kasa kɔkɔbɔ no ho asɛm
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, sɛ yɛbɛka kɔkɔbɔ no ho asɛm a, yɛnka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm: 'Mɛtrɛ a 7, mɛde abɔ ne mɛfa akɔ ada pa'. Wɔ English mu, yɛnka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm wɔ ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm: 'I get up at 7, have breakfast and go to work'. Nnipa no ho asɛm no, wɔ English mu yɛnka 'at' ma wɔde bɛka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm ('at 7 o'clock'), 'in' ma wɔde bɛka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm ('in the morning') ne 'on' ma wɔde bɛka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm ('on Monday'). Yɛnka nso adverbials a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm sɛ 'always', 'usually', 'sometimes' ma wɔde bɛka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm.
rule: Sɛ wubɛka kɔkɔbɔ no ho asɛm a: 1) Nka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm (I get up, she works). 2) Nka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm: 'at' + ɛno (at 8 am), 'in' + ɛno (in the morning), 'on' + ɛno (on Friday). 3) Nka adverbials a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm ma wɔde bɛka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm (I always eat breakfast). 4) Sɛ wubɛka asɛm a, ka sɛ: 'What time do you get up?' anaa 'When do you have lunch?'

concept_examples.text: She usually has breakfast at 8 am.
concept_examples.translation: Ɔbaa no daa de abɔ a 8 a ɛnneɛ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː ˈjuːʒuəli hæz ˈbrekfəst æt eɪt æm/

concept_examples.text: We go to work at 9 in the morning.
concept_examples.translation: Yɛfa akɔ ada pa a 9 a ɛnneɛ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː ɡəʊ tə wɜːk æt naɪn ɪn ðə ˈmɔːnɪŋ/

concept_examples.text: What time do you have dinner?

common_error.wrong: I am eating breakfast every morning.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛnka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm ma wɔde bɛka aɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm ('estoy desayunando cada mañana'), nanso wɔ English mu, ma wɔde bɛka kɔkɔbɔ ne nnwoma no ho asɛm a, yɛnka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm, ɛnte saa ɛno biara.

examples.note: Verb wɔ ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm ma wɔde bɛka kɔkɔbɔ no ho asɛm.

levels.label: Time expressions
levels.translation: ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm

examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv lʌntʃ æt wʌn piː em/
examples.note: Yɛnka 'at' ma wɔde bɛka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm.

levels.label: Frequency adverbs
levels.translation: Adverbials a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm

examples.translation: Ɔbaa no mmom ntɛm nyɛ adadesɛm.
examples.note: Adverbial a wɔde bɛka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm ma wɔde bɛka ɛno a wɔde bɛka aɛno ho asɛm.

levels.label: Questions about routines
levels.translation: Asɛm a wɔbɛka kɔkɔbɔ no ho

examples.original: What time do you go to bed?
examples.phonetic: /wɒt taɪm duː juː ɡəʊ tə bed/
examples.translation: ɛbɛyɛ dɛn a wotrɛ a wɔnntɛm?
examples.note: Asɛm a wɔbɛka 'what time' + do/does.

title: Kyerε ma wopɛ ne wopɛn (Mepɛ / Mempɛ)
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, sε yɛbɛka yɛn pɛ, yɛnka asɛm 'pɛ' ne 'te': 'Mepɛ pizza' (siesie 'Pizza pɛ me'). Wɔ English mu, yɛnka asɛm 'like' ne abusuo + like + εberε: 'I like pizza'. Nnipa no ara ne sɛ wɔ Twi mu, asɛm 'pɛ' kyerε εberε no (me pɛ pizza, me pɛ pizzas), na wɔ English mu 'like' kyerε abusuo no (I like pizza, He likes pizza). Nso, hwɛ sɛ wopɛ wɔka sɛ wopɛn, ka sɛ 'I don't like' (mempɛ).
rule: Sɛ wopɛ wɔka pɛ: 1) Kyerεkyerε: I/you/we/they like + εberε (I like coffee). He/she/it likes + εberε (She likes coffee). 2) Mmemmɛ: I/you/we/they don't like (I don't like tea). He/she/it doesn't like (He doesn't like tea). 3) Asɛm a wɔrekyekyer: Do you like...? (Wopɛ...?), Does she like...? (Wopɛ no...?). 4) Sɛ wopɛ wɔka kyerε sɛ wopɛ paa: 'I like it very much' (Mepɛ no paa) anaa 'I really like it' (Mepɛ no paa).

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi mu, asɛm 'paa' baa asɛm no mu: 'Mepɛ pizza paa'. Wɔ English mu, asɛm 'very much' baa kyerεkyerɛ no mu anaa εberε no nkyɛn: 'I like pizza very much'. Sɛ wode no ntɛm asɛm no ne εberε no a, εyɛ akannya.

examples.note: Asɛm 'like' wɔ asɛm no mu.
Yɛde -s ka ho wɔ krataa no mu.
Yɛnka 'doesn't' + asɛm no mu.
Asɛm a wɔrekyekyer ne 'do' + abusuo + asɛm no mu.

title: Ask for and give prices
bridge: Wɔ Twi akyi, sɛ yɛbisa asɛm deε ne 'Ɛyɛ pegyɛn biara?' anaa 'Ɛyɛ pegyɛn sɛn?' Wɔ English akyi, yɛse 'How much is it?' (kwan) anaa 'How much are they?' (mmara). Yɛnkyerɛ biara ne sɛ wɔ English akyi yɛnka 'to be' anaa 'cost' ne abɔdeε 'does' sɛ yɛbisa. Sɛ yɛde asɛm deε a, yɛse 'It is [nipa] dollars/euros' anaa 'It costs [nipa].'
rule: Sɛ wabisa asɛm deε: 1) 'How much is it?' (sɛ yɛwɔ kwan biara) anaa 'How much are they?' (sɛ yɛwɔ mmara). 2) 'How much does it cost?' (Ɛyɛ pegyɛn biara?). 3) 'How much is the T-shirt?' (Ɛyɛ pegyɛn biara ne T-shirt?). Sɛ wade asɛm deε a, wase 'It is 25 dollars' anaa 'It costs 25 dollars'. Wɔ mmemmɛm a, yɛnka 'to be' anaa abɔdeε 'does' ne 'cost'.

concept_examples.translation: Ɛyɛ pegyɛn sɛn ne nsroma no?

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi akyi, yɛse 'Ɛyɛ pegyɛn biara?' anaa 'Ɛyɛ pegyɛn sɛn?' anaa 'Ɛyɛ pegyɛn sɛn ne nsroma no?' ansa na wɔ English akyi, sɛ yɛka 'cost', yɛntɔm abɔdeε 'does' sɛ yɛbisa. Ɛyɛ kwan kɔkɔ a wɔ Hispanicfoɔ nni.

examples.translation: Ɛyɛ pegyɛn biara ne nwoma no?
examples.note: Yɛnka 'to be' sɛ yɛbisa asɛm deε.

examples.original: How much does the bag cost?
examples.translation: Ɛyɛ pegyɛn biara ne bag no?
examples.note: Yɛnka 'does' ne 'cost' sɛ yɛbisa.
Yɛnka 'costs' wɔ nipa a ɛyɛ kwan biara.

examples.translation: Ɛyɛ pegyɛn sɛn ne mmra no?
examples.note: Yɛnka 'are' wɔ mmara akyi.

title: Kyerεw wo a wɔ akyerε mu
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, sε yɛbɛka wɔn a wɔ wɔ akyerε mu, yɛka 'Wɔ wɔ mu...', 'Wɔ wɔ bank no akyi', 'Wɔ wɔ bus stop no nkyɛn'. Wɔ English mu, yɛnka 'on', 'in', 'at', 'next to', 'near', 'opposite', 'behind', 'in front of'. Nnipa a wɔka Twi no adwene yɛ den na wɔn a wɔka Twi no nea wɔka so ara na wɔde 'en' ka biribiara, na wɔ English mu, sɛnea wɔde preposition ka no kyerɛɛ context no so. Nso, ma wo hu a, sɛ yɛbɛka wɔn a wɔ wɔ akyerε mu, yɛde 'to be' (It is...).
rule: Sɛ wubɛka wɔn a wɔ wɔ akyerε mu: 1) De 'to be' (The bank is...). 2) Prepositions: 'on' (wɔ mu anaa wɔ to a wɔ ase), 'in' (wɔ mu), 'at' (wɔ akyerε bi mu), 'next to' (akyi), 'near' (nkyɛn), 'opposite' (ntɛm), 'behind' (ho), 'in front of' (anim). 3) Sɛ wubɛka asɛm: 'Where is the...?' anaa 'Is there a... near here?'.

concept_examples.text: The supermarket is near the park.
concept_examples.translation: Super market no wɔ park no nkyɛn.

concept_examples.text: The school is next to the church.
concept_examples.translation: School no wɔ church no akyi.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðə skuːl ɪz nekst tə ðə tʃɜːtʃ/

concept_examples.text: The pharmacy is on Main Street.
concept_examples.translation: Pharmacy no wɔ Main Street so.

common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛka 'Wɔ wɔ corner no so' na yɛntɔ subject no. Wɔ English mu, subject 'It' anaa 'He/She' no yɛ nokware. Nso, 'en la esquina' yɛ 'on the corner' (entɔ 'in the corner') sɛ wɔ wɔ streets no ntɛm.

examples.original: The cat is in the garden.
examples.translation: Cat no wɔ garden no mu.
examples.note: Yɛde 'in' ka wɔn a wɔ mu.

examples.original: The restaurant is next to the hotel.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈrestrɒnt ɪz nekst tə ðə həʊˈtel/
examples.translation: Restaurant no wɔ hotel no akyi.
examples.note: Yɛde 'next to' ka wɔn a wɔ akyi.

examples.original: The bank is opposite the park.
examples.translation: Bank no wɔ park no ntɛm.
examples.note: Yɛde 'opposite' ka wɔn a wɔ ntɛm.
Sɛw a wɔde 'Where' ka.
